title: Burst Balloons
source: canonical Burst Balloons concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of positive integers, one balloon per position. Bursting the balloon at position i scores the product of its value with the values of the balloons still standing immediately to its left and right; after neighbors burst, the ends count as value 1. Burst every balloon and return the largest total score possible by choosing the order well.

examples.explanation: Burst 2 first for 1 x 2 x 4 = 8, then 4 alone for 1 x 4 x 1 = 4.
A single balloon scores its own value against the two virtual ends.

hints: Think about the LAST balloon burst in a range, not the first: when it bursts, its two sides no longer interact.
Add a virtual 1 at each end. For an open range between positions left and right, try every interior balloon as the last one burst.
Table over ranges: best(left, right) = max over k inside of best(left, k) + best(k, right) + values[left] * values[k] * values[right].
solution: Interval DP with virtual ends: for every open range, the last balloon burst inside it splits the problem in two independent sides, so try each interior balloon as the last and take the best. O(n^3) time, O(n^2) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include a single balloon, two balloons, and a weak balloon between strong neighbors
